## From raw mass spectra and quantitative proteomes to biological insight

**ProtVis** combines raw-data database search, heterogeneous quantitative proteomics import, preprocessing, data summary, statistical analysis, functional interpretation, multi-omics integration, PTM analysis, and publication-ready visualization in one interactive workflow. This cookbook follows the application in the same order that a real project is analyzed.

[Start with installation](content/installation.qmd) · [Prepare RAW → mzML](content/data_import/msconvert_raw_to_mzml.qmd) · [Run Raw/mzML + Sage](content/data_import/raw_sage_search.qmd) · [Understand `ProtVis_dataset`](content/reproducibility/ProtVis_dataset.qmd)
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Documentation version
This edition is aligned to **ProtVis 0.7.9 on the `dev` branch**. ProtVis is under active development; the cookbook emphasizes stable concepts and explicitly identifies compatibility behavior where relevant.
:::

## ProtVis at a glance

The updated overview shows the two principal data-entry routes supported by ProtVis. **Raw `.mzML` files plus FASTA** enter through **Sage search**, while **mainstream proteomics software outputs** and a **user-defined quantitative matrix** enter through their corresponding import routes. Both routes converge on the same `ProtVis_dataset`, which then connects preprocessing, data summary, downstream analysis, multi-omics/WGCNA, and key-protein characterization.

The Data input stage contains a raw mzML plus FASTA route through Sage search and a quantitative route for mainstream proteomics software outputs and user-defined matrices. Both feed ProtVis_dataset. Data pre-processing includes noise correction, data transformation, missing-value imputation, and normalization. Data summary includes sample correlation, expression heatmap, and dimensionality reduction before and after normalization. Downstream data analysis includes differential abundance analysis, functional enrichment, GSEA, and pathway analysis. Multi-omics analysis includes K-means clustering, nine-quadrant analysis, co-enrichment, and WGCNA. Key-protein characterization covers sequence-based functional analyses, protein structure and interactions, and modifications including phosphorylation, acetylation, methylation, and glycosylation." width="100%" fig-align="center"}

<div class="feature-grid">
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>Raw mzML + FASTA</strong>
<p>Convert vendor RAW files to mzML when needed, register sample metadata and FASTA, then run Sage search to generate peptide/protein evidence and a quantitative matrix.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>Mainstream software outputs</strong>
<p>Import quantitative results from MaxQuant, Proteome Discoverer, DIA-NN, Spectronaut, FragPipe, Skyline, OpenMS, Mascot, or a user-defined matrix.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>Unified ProtVis_dataset</strong>
<p>Both input routes converge on <code>ProtVis_dataset</code>, which keeps quantitative data, metadata, annotations, analysis results, source files, parameters, and process history together.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>Data pre-processing</strong>
<p>Correct replicate-level noise, transform intensities, inspect and impute missing values, and normalize the quantitative matrix before downstream analysis.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>Data summary</strong>
<p>Assess sample correlation, expression patterns, and dimensionality reduction before and after normalization to evaluate data structure and preprocessing effects.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>Downstream data analysis</strong>
<p>Perform differential abundance analysis and continue into functional enrichment, GSEA, and pathway analysis for biological interpretation.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>Multi-omics and WGCNA</strong>
<p>Use K-means expression profiling, nine-quadrant integration, co-enrichment, WGCNA, and related modules to connect multiple molecular layers and identify coordinated modules.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature-card">
<strong>Key-protein characterization</strong>
<p>Move from selected proteins to sequence-based functional analysis, subcellular localization, secondary/tertiary structure, protein-protein interactions, and PTM-oriented characterization.</p>
</div>
</div>

## Recommended analysis paths

For **vendor RAW data**, first convert the files to mzML using the platform-specific RAW → mzML tutorial, then use:

**RAW → mzML → Project init → Search (Sage) → Correct Noise → Data Transformation → Data Imputation → Data Normalization → Overview → DEP → Interpretation**

For **already-converted mzML + FASTA**, start directly from:

**Project init → Search (Sage) → Correct Noise → Data Transformation → Data Imputation → Data Normalization → Overview → DEP → Interpretation**

For **MaxQuant**, use:

**Project init → MaxQuant Output Preparation → Correct Noise → Data Transformation → Data Imputation → Data Normalization → Overview → DEP → Interpretation**

For **other supported tabular outputs**, import or parse the source-specific quantitative table and continue into the shared preprocessing workflow.

The Raw route is intentionally different: Project init can create a sample-only Sage staging `ProtVis_dataset` without inventing an expression matrix. The protein-by-sample matrix is created only after the Sage LFQ search succeeds. In contrast, software-derived quantitative tables enter with an expression matrix already available and then converge on the same preprocessing and downstream architecture.

## Two ways to learn ProtVis

**GUI-first users** can follow the chapter order in the sidebar. Each page explains prerequisites, the controls to use, expected outputs, and common failure points.

**Reproducible-workflow users** should also read [`ProtVis_dataset`](content/reproducibility/ProtVis_dataset.qmd) and [Checkpoints & recovery](content/reproducibility/checkpoints.qmd). These chapters explain how ProtVis preserves analysis provenance and how projects can be resumed without rebuilding every previous step.
